newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse edges up on gains to VSZ shares.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse edges up on gains to VSZ shares.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with gains to shares of VSZ steel pushing the SAX index up 0.31 points to 206.79.
VSZ rose 25 crowns to close at 750 and brokers said demand continued to outstrip supply.

"The demand for VSZ share continues, but shareholders appear to be waiting until the price climbs higher, maybe to around 800 crowns, where they could sell their holdings and where you could buy a larger package," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
"(But) the market lacks a strong impetus to put it on a long-term track...and it also lacks a wide range of issues to deserve a more important place in foreign investor portfolios," he added.
Brokers said they did not expect the sluggish sentiment on the bourse to end in the near future.
They said that even though some shares were undervalued compared to similar issues in the region, even blue chips such as Slovnaft or drug maker Slovakofarma lacked liquidity for more active trading.
Oil refiner Slovnaft dropped two crowns to close at 1,004, but traded only 69 shares.
Overall volume fell to 178,703 shares, from 204,788 stocks on Wednesday, while turnover rose to 80.72 million crowns, from 56.81 million.
